events.text: The rains have broken a channel high on the rice terraces, and the water is pouring down the wrong side of the hill. A Miao farmer is shouting up at the slope as if it could hear him.

choices.text: Climb up and rebuild the channel

ok.log: Stones, mud and an afternoon of it. The water finds its way again, and the farmer sends a basket of red rice after you.

fail.log: The bank gives way under you and you ride the mud halfway down the hill. The farmer laughs until he cries, then helps you up.

choices.text: Show him how to cut a spillway

ok.log: A spillway, two bamboo pipes, a terrace saved. The whole village comes to look at it, and at you.

fail.log: Your spillway floods the terrace below instead. You spend the evening apologising to another farmer.

choices.text: Leave the hill to the hill

effects.log: You watch the water take a terrace that took ten years to build, and walk on quietly.

events.text: It is the festival of the new rice, and the girls of the village are dancing in so much silver that they ring when they turn. The boys are blowing reed pipes taller than themselves. Someone pushes a pipe into your hands.

choices.text: Blow the pipe as hard as you can

effects.log: A noise like a goose comes out. The whole square cheers, and an old man shows you where to put your fingers.

choices.text: Join the line of dancers

ok.log: You keep the steps all the way round the square. A grandmother ties a little silver bell to your sleeve.

fail.log: You turn left when everyone turns right. Nobody minds. You are dancing, and that is what counts.

choices.text: Watch from the steps

effects.log: You watch the silver flash in the torchlight until you fall asleep against a post.

events.text: A Miao grandmother with a basket of leaves on her back stops you at the edge of the forest and makes you name every plant on the path. You know two.

choices.text: Ask her to teach you the rest

effects.log: By sunset you know which leaf for a bite, which for a fever and which for a liar. She will not explain the last one.

choices.text: Carry her basket home for her

effects.log: The basket weighs more than you do. At her door she gives you a pinch of something that tastes of pepper and makes you sleep like a stone.

choices.text: Run off before the lesson starts

effects.log: She calls after you that the red-veined one bites back. You find out which one that is a week later.

events.text: Under the stilt house, in the wet shade, there is a fat golden toad that the grown-ups say brings luck to whoever catches it and bad luck to whoever keeps it.

choices.text: Catch it and let it go again

ok.log: It sits in your two hands for a moment like a little warm coin. Then it is gone, and the luck, you hope, is not.

fail.log: It leaves a stripe of something sticky on your hand that itches for two days.

choices.text: Catch it and keep it in a jar

effects.log: The toad sulks. That week you fall out of a tree, lose a tooth and break a bowl. You let it go.

choices.text: Leave it in its shade

effects.log: The toad blinks at you, slowly, like an old man approving.

events.text: At the Sisters' Meal festival the young women of the valley cook rice in five colours and hand it, wrapped in leaves, to the guests they like. Hidden inside each parcel is a sign: chopsticks, a pine needle, a chilli.

choices.text: Accept a parcel and open it

effects.log: Inside is a pine needle, which means come back next year. Everyone says so at once, and laughs.

choices.text: Sing a song across the valley in answer

ok.log: Your song carries to the far slope and a song comes back. By the end of the night you are the guest everyone wants.

fail.log: Your song carries to the far slope and the far slope goes quiet. A kind cousin explains the words you got wrong.

choices.text: Help the old women at the fires

effects.log: You stir rice until your arms ache. The old women decide you are a sensible sort.

events.text: You put your foot into your boot in the morning and something inside it moves. Something long, and cool, and very still now.

choices.text: Freeze, and let it leave on its own

ok.log: You know the pattern on its back: a krait, asleep and cross. You wait, breathing like a stone, and it pours itself out and away.

fail.log: It bites on the way out. The village healer works over you through the night, and you live, and you look in your boots for the rest of your life.

choices.text: Kick the boot away hard

effects.log: The boot flies, the snake flies, and both land in the cook pot. The cook does not speak to you for a week.

choices.text: Call for the Miao boy next door

effects.log: He lifts it out with two sticks, laughing at you, and carries it off to sell to the poison clans.

events.text: A cooking fire has got into the thatch of a stilt house at the end of the village. Under it, the pigs are screaming; inside it, someone is shouting for a child.

choices.text: Go up the ladder into the smoke

ok.log: You come down with the child under one arm and your hair smouldering. The village will tell this for years.

fail.log: The ladder burns through under you. You fall into the pig pen with the child safe on top of you.

choices.text: Run the bucket line from the stream

effects.log: The house is lost, the child is found under the granary, and you are black to the elbows.

choices.text: Keep your distance

effects.log: You watch from the path. A woman passing gives you a long look.

events.text: Three days into the deep forest the leeches have found you, the rain has not stopped and a fever is climbing your spine. The trail ahead goes down into a valley full of white mist.

choices.text: Push on through the mist

ok.log: You walk the fever out of yourself and come down into a valley of wild orchids nobody has picked. You sit among them for a day.

fail.log: The mist is the fever and the fever is the mist. A Hani woodcutter finds you asleep in a stream and carries you out.

choices.text: Brew the bark the grandmothers use

ok.log: Bitter as old regrets. The fever breaks in the night, and you wake up hungry.

fail.log: Wrong bark. You spend the night being sick, and the fever passes anyway, out of boredom.

choices.text: Turn back to the village

effects.log: You come out of the forest thinner and wiser, and the forest does not seem to mind.

events.text: Wild elephants have come down out of the forest into the banana groves in the night, a whole herd with calves, and the village is beating gongs from the rooftops. The elephants are not impressed.

choices.text: Walk out and lead them off with salt

ok.log: The old cow follows the salt, the herd follows the cow, and by dawn they are a grey line going back into the trees.

fail.log: The old cow follows the salt, and then you, fast. You spend the morning up a palm tree.

choices.text: Help carry the grain up into the lofts

effects.log: The elephants eat the bananas and leave the rice. The village counts it a good night.

choices.text: Watch them from a safe roof

effects.log: A calf plays in the irrigation ditch until its mother lifts it out by the tail. You never forget it.

events.text: A Tea Horse Road merchant is pressing aged tea into bricks in the market of Pu'er, and offers you a share of a mule string going north: "Carry and guard, or buy and wait."

choices.text: Buy a stack of tea bricks (40 taels)

effects.log: You store the bricks under your bed. A year later a Tibetan trader pays you twice what they cost.

choices.text: Guard the mule string a stretch

ok.log: Thieves try the string on the second pass and change their minds. The merchant pays you in silver and tea.

fail.log: You lose a mule and most of your dignity in a ravine. The merchant pays you a little, out of pity.

choices.text: Drink a bowl with him and go

effects.log: Dark tea, older than you. It settles something in your chest.

events.text: On Erhai Lake under the mountains of Dali, a fisherman with a raft full of cormorants is having a bad day. His birds have caught nothing but each other.

choices.text: Help him read the water

ok.log: You see the shoal moving under the light on the water. By noon the raft is full of silver fish and the birds are smug.

fail.log: You point at shadows. The birds look at you with contempt. The fisherman shares his rice anyway.

choices.text: Sit on the raft and watch the mountains

effects.log: Snow on the peaks, wind on the lake, a bird drying its wings beside you. You breathe easier for a month.

choices.text: Buy his catch for the inn (10 taels)

effects.log: The inn cooks it in sour broth. It is the best meal of the year.

events.text: A Han tax collector with six soldiers is in a Miao village demanding a silver tax the village has already paid. The headman has the receipt in his hand. The collector will not read it.

choices.text: Read the receipt aloud to the soldiers

ok.log: The soldiers look at each other, then at the collector. He leaves with nothing, and the village gives you a silver comb.

fail.log: The collector has you thrown in the mud for your trouble. The village pays, and remembers you tried.

choices.text: Pay the second tax for them (30 taels)

effects.log: The headman accepts it with a face like stone. That night the whole village eats at his house, and you with them.

choices.text: Stay out of a quarrel with the court

effects.log: You keep walking. Behind you, the headman folds the receipt very small.

events.text: In the Stone Forest, among grey pillars taller than temples, an old swordsman is practising alone. His blade never touches the stone, and he never stops.

choices.text: Watch until he stops

effects.log: He stops at dusk, after four hours, and says without turning round: "The stone does not move. That is the lesson." It is.

choices.text: Ask him to spar

ok.log: You last nine exchanges. He nods, which you suspect is the most he has ever done for anyone.

fail.log: You last two. He shows you why, slowly, three times.

choices.text: Leave him to his stones

effects.log: You walk out of the maze of pillars by moonlight. You could swear the stones had moved.

events.text: It is the mushroom season, and the whole province has gone into the pine woods with baskets. A woman at the market is selling one kind that, she says cheerfully, makes you see little men dancing.

choices.text: Sort the good from the strange

ok.log: You pick out the bad ones at a glance, and the market starts bringing you baskets to check.

fail.log: You eat the wrong one. For a whole afternoon the little men dance on your rice bowl. They are very good dancers.

choices.text: Buy a basket of the good ones (15 taels)

effects.log: Fried with chilli and garlic. You understand at last why the province goes mad every summer.

choices.text: Go picking in the woods yourself

effects.log: You find a ring of yellow caps under a pine and sell them for a handful of silver.

events.text: The road into the Southern Wilds crosses a gorge on a bridge of rope and bamboo. A Miao boy sits at the end of it with a tally stick and asks every traveller the same question: "Do you come as a guest, or as a buyer of poison?"

choices.text: Answer "As a guest"

effects.log: He grins and waves you over. On the far side, someone has already been told you are coming.

choices.text: Answer "As a buyer"

effects.log: He looks at you a long moment, then points you to a different path. It is steeper, and watched.

choices.text: Cross without answering

ok.log: The bridge swings, you do not. On the far side nobody greets you at all.

fail.log: Halfway over, the bridge decides to teach you manners. You arrive soaked from the spray and shaking.

events.text: On the red-earth road a Naxi muleteer is kneeling by a mule that has eaten something from the verge, and the mule is shaking.

choices.text: Treat the mule

ok.log: You know the leaf it ate and the leaf that answers it. The mule is up by dusk, and the muleteer will not let you pay for anything.

fail.log: You do no good, and no harm. The mule recovers by itself in the night, which the muleteer credits to you anyway.

choices.text: Help him unload and wait

effects.log: You sit with him through the night. He tells you the whole road, every pass and inn, from here to Lhasa.

choices.text: Walk on

effects.log: Behind you the muleteer starts to sing to the mule, low and steady.

events.text: On the fifth night of the fifth month your sect lights the five great cauldrons in the temple yard. Every disciple must feed one of them through the night, and the fires must not change colour.

choices.text: Take the snake cauldron, the hardest

ok.log: The green flame holds until dawn. The elders say nothing, which in this sect is praise, and write your name in the merit book.

fail.log: The flame goes yellow before dawn and you breathe the smoke. You spend three days in the infirmary, and the elders spend them watching you.

choices.text: Take the toad cauldron with a junior

effects.log: You teach the junior to read the smoke. By morning the fire is steady and so is the child.

choices.text: Keep watch over the gate instead

effects.log: Somebody has to. The night is long and quiet, and the cauldrons behind you burn five colours.

events.text: An elder of your sect with a centipede tattooed around one wrist sets a bowl of grey mist in front of you. "Breathe it out of yourself," she says, "and never breathe it back in."

choices.text: Try the Hundred-Legged Mist

ok.log: The mist walks where you send it and nowhere else. The elder grunts and teaches you the second half.

fail.log: The mist walks back to you. You cough for a month, and understand it better for it.

choices.text: Ask her what it is for

effects.log: "For when they come up the valley with torches," she says. "It has happened before." You do not ask again.

choices.text: Ask to learn the cure first

effects.log: She looks at you properly for the first time. "Good," she says, and teaches you that.

events.text: Envoys from an orthodox sect are at the temple gate with a dead dog and a jar of well water. A town on the Red River is sick, they say, and everyone knows who poisons wells.

choices.text: Test the water before them all

ok.log: Not poison: a dead buffalo upstream, rotting. You ride down with them and pull it out. The envoys bow, stiffly, and go home with a story they did not expect.

fail.log: You cannot name it, and that is as good as a confession to them. They leave cursing your sect, and the town stays sick.

choices.text: Send cures to the town without a word

effects.log: Your sect's cures go down the river on a raft. The town gets better. Nobody says who sent them, and everybody knows.

choices.text: Shut the gate on them

effects.log: Let them think what they think. They do, loudly, all the way back to the Central Plains.

events.text: Your sect's cures are as famous as its poisons, and on market day the temple steps are crowded with the bitten, the fevered and the merely frightened. Some of them can pay.

choices.text: Charge what the cures are worth

effects.log: The sect's coffers fill, and the elders note who brought it in.

choices.text: Treat the poor for nothing

effects.log: All day, for nothing. In the villages they start to say your name in the same breath as the toad shrine.

choices.text: Spend the day watching the healers work

effects.log: You learn more from one old healer's hands than from a year of manuals.

events.text: You are bitten by a scorpion on a jungle path and do not die, which surprises the woman in indigo and silver who was watching from the trees. "Most outsiders do," she says. "The Five Poisons Sect could use someone like you."

choices.text: Follow her to the Five Poisons Sect

effects.log: She leads you up a valley full of green mist to a temple of carved black stone. You are a disciple of the Five Poisons Sect now, and your blood, they say, has already passed the first trial.

choices.text: Ask her for the cure, not the gate

effects.log: She laughs and gives you a leaf to chew. "Come back when you are bored of being ordinary."

choices.text: Walk away holding your arm

effects.log: She lets you go. The bite swells for a week. You think about her offer more than you expected.

events.text: A fever is going through the valley villages of Shuangjiang, and the Han magistrate in the market town has posted a notice: the Miao poison clans are to blame. Up on the hill, in a stilt house hung with silver, old Ou Lan, the healer every village sends for, is the only one still working. "I need hands," she says, "and somebody the soldiers will let pass."

choices.text: Offer her your hands

effects.log: She sets you to grinding roots and boiling water. By morning you know the names of the sick, and the smell of the fever.

choices.text: Ask what the fever really is

ok.log: You see it at once: a marsh fever, not a poison. Ou Lan nods slowly. "You see. Then you can help."

fail.log: You cannot tell. Ou Lan says it does not matter, and puts a pestle in your hand.

choices.text: Keep clear of the trouble

effects.log: You go down the other side of the hill. Behind you the valley coughs through the night.

events.text: The fever is winning. Ou Lan sends her grandson Ou Daqing and you into the deep forest for the one flower that breaks it, a white orchid that grows only on the cliffs of the Gorge of Nine Mists. Daqing is fifteen and frightened, and pretending not to be.

choices.text: Climb for the orchids yourself

ok.log: You come down the wet cliff with both hands full. Daqing looks at you as if you had come down from the sky.

fail.log: You fall the last stretch and break the fall with your shoulder. But the orchids are in your shirt, and whole.

choices.text: Teach Daqing to climb it

ok.log: He climbs it with your voice under him the whole way. At the top he whoops so loud the birds leave the gorge.

fail.log: He freezes halfway. You go up after him and bring down him and the orchids both, the slow way.

events.text: You come back down the valley with the orchids to find soldiers at the foot of Ou Lan's hill. Magistrate Qiu Wenbo has decided that a Miao grandmother brewing pots at night is the poisoner, and has come with torches to burn her house. "Hand over the witch's pots," he tells you, "and I will pay for your trouble."

choices.text: Stand in front of the ladder

ok.log: The first two soldiers go into the paddy. The rest decide this is not their quarrel. The magistrate backs away with his torch shaking.

fail.log: They knock you down, but not before the orchids are up the ladder. Ou Lan brews through the night while you lie bruised under her house.

choices.text: Prove to him it is a marsh fever

ok.log: You walk him to the marsh and show him the sick who never drank from a Miao well. He goes red, then white, and sends his soldiers home.

fail.log: He does not follow a word, but he is unsure now, and an unsure man with a torch waits. It is enough time for Ou Lan.

choices.text: Take his silver and hand over a pot

effects.log: He pays you 60 taels and smashes the pot in the square. The cure in it was half made. Ou Lan does not look at you.

events.text: The fever breaks at the turn of the season. The valleys of Shuangjiang send Ou Lan pigs, rice and silver, and she sends half of it on to you. When the magistrate is recalled, the villages hold a feast with you at the high end of the table, and an old man sings a long song in Miao in which, Daqing tells you, you climb a cliff made of clouds.

choices.text: Take the silver comb she offers

effects.log: A comb of old silver, worn smooth by four generations of hands. You carry it all your life, and something of this valley with it.

choices.text: Ask her to teach you the fever cure

effects.log: She teaches you all winter. Much later, in other places, you will save lives with what she showed you.

choices.text: Leave quietly before the feast ends

effects.log: You slip out under the songs. In the morning there is a sack of red rice on your doorstep with a silver bell tied to it.

events.text: A year on, the valleys of Shuangjiang still talk about the fever and the stranger who sold Ou Lan's pot to the magistrate. Ou Lan lived; three of her patients did not. On the road you meet Ou Daqing, taller now, with a basket of leaves on his back. He stops when he sees you.

choices.text: Apologise to him, properly

ok.log: He hears you out. He does not forgive you, but he tells you which leaf his grandmother uses for a heavy heart, and walks on.

fail.log: He walks past as if you were a tree. You stand on the road a long time.

choices.text: Send silver to the families (50 taels)

effects.log: You leave 50 taels with the headman for the three families. It buys no forgiveness, but it buys rice.

choices.text: Say nothing and pass him by

effects.log: Neither of you says anything. The valley has a long memory, and now it has you in it.

events.text: In the market of a Yunnan border town a smooth-voiced pedlar named Pan Shou is selling little black pills against "every bite of the Southern Wilds". He has a scroll with a toad seal on it, and a crowd.

choices.text: Buy a pill and test it (10 taels)

effects.log: You crush it in the inn that night. Soot, honey and a little pepper. Nothing that would stop anything.

choices.text: Look closely at his toad seal

ok.log: The seal is carved backwards. Whoever made it had only ever seen it in a mirror. Pan Shou sees you looking.

fail.log: It looks real to you. You walk on, and buy nothing, which is something.

choices.text: Walk past the crowd

effects.log: A woman beside you buys ten pills for her husband, who works in the cane fields.

events.text: Two weeks later a cane cutter is carried into town with a viper bite and a pocket full of Pan Shou's pills. He took them all. The healer is out in the hills, and the man's wife is looking at you, because you were the one who asked about the seal.

choices.text: Treat the bite yourself

ok.log: You cut nothing, bind it right and keep him still all night. He lives. His wife tells the whole market where the pills came from.

fail.log: You keep him alive until the healer comes back at dawn, and no further, but it is enough. He lives, and limps.

choices.text: Run for the healer in the hills

ok.log: You find her by moonlight and bring her down at a run. The man lives.

fail.log: You find her too late for his leg, in time for the rest of him.

events.text: You track Pan Shou to a rope-bridge village where he is selling the same pills to a Miao clan, under their own toad seal. The clan elders are beginning to understand. Pan Shou sees you across the square and goes white, then smiles. "Friend," he says quietly, "half of everything, and you never saw me."

choices.text: Tell the elders everything

ok.log: The elders listen. Pan Shou is walked to the bridge and told never to cross it again. The clan gives you a place at their fire.

fail.log: The elders do not trust a stranger's word any more than his. But they stop buying, and Pan Shou leaves by night.

choices.text: Stop him on the bridge

ok.log: He tries a knife and finds out what a murim fighter is. You hand him to the elders over the swinging bridge.

fail.log: He throws pepper in your eyes and is across the bridge, but he drops his whole bag of pills. The clan burns them.

choices.text: Take his offer

effects.log: He pays you 80 taels from a fat purse and is gone by morning. The pills go on selling, under the toad seal.

events.text: The clan whose seal Pan Shou forged sends a boy down to find you, with a gift wrapped in a banana leaf and a message: their healers have made real pills, with the right seal, and want the markets to know whose word to trust.

choices.text: Carry the true pills to the markets

effects.log: You walk them through four towns. Wherever you go, the cane cutters ask for "the pills the stranger brought".

choices.text: Open the gift

effects.log: A small jar of the clan's best snakebite salve. You will be glad of it more than once.

choices.text: Send the boy back with thanks

effects.log: The boy goes back up the mountain proud. The clan's door is open to you from now on.

events.text: Pan Shou's pills have reached the lowlands, and a child in a river town has died of a scorpion sting with three of them in her hand. Somebody remembers the stranger who was seen drinking with the pedlar.

choices.text: Hunt Pan Shou down at last

ok.log: You find him in a teahouse in Kunming and take him to the magistrate with his own purse as evidence. It does not bring the child back.

fail.log: He is gone into the south, beyond the borders. You never find him. You never stop looking either.

choices.text: Give his silver to the river town (80 taels)

effects.log: You hand over all 80 taels to the child's family. They take it. They do not thank you.

choices.text: Leave the province for a while

effects.log: You take the road north into Sichuan. The Southern Wilds will be there when you are ready.

events.text: A Miao girl of sixteen named Ah Yao is keeping a spider in a bamboo tube under her bed, and a centipede in another, and a toad, a scorpion and a snake. Her clan are healers and want her to be one. She wants to pass the trial of the Five Poisons Sect, and she has asked you, of all people, to keep the secret.
events.arc: The Girl Who Wanted the Fifth Poison

choices.text: Keep her secret

effects.log: She shows you her five tubes with enormous pride, one by one. The snake bites her. She does not cry.

choices.text: Help her train in the forest

ok.log: You teach her to read the colours of a bite. She learns it faster than you did.

fail.log: You teach her wrong, and the scorpion teaches you both right. You laugh about it through swollen hands.

choices.text: Tell her grandmother

effects.log: The tubes are emptied into the forest. Ah Yao does not speak to you again.

events.text: Ah Yao's grandmother finds the tubes. There is shouting in three languages, and then Ah Yao is at your door with a bundle and a cut lip from the bamboo door frame. The trial of the Five Poisons Sect is at the next new moon, three valleys away.
events.arc: The Girl Who Wanted the Fifth Poison

choices.text: Walk her to the trial

effects.log: Three valleys, two rope bridges and a night in a cave. She talks the whole way. You find you are proud of her.

choices.text: Talk to the grandmother first

ok.log: The grandmother hears you out. She gives Ah Yao a silver bracelet for luck and says she must come home to visit. Ah Yao cries for the first time.

fail.log: The grandmother does not listen. You walk Ah Yao to the trial anyway, and the village looks at you sideways after.

events.text: At the trial in the green mist, the Five Poisons Sect sets each candidate a bowl with five venoms in it and one cure, and an hour to find which is which. Ah Yao's hands are shaking. One of the other candidates, a rich boy from the lowlands, is quietly switching bowls.
events.arc: The Girl Who Wanted the Fifth Poison

choices.text: Call out the cheat before the elders

ok.log: The elders look, nod, and send the boy home in his own palanquin. Ah Yao gets her own bowl back, and finds the cure with a minute to spare.

fail.log: Nobody believes a stranger at the edge of the yard. But the boy is rattled, and Ah Yao is not, and that is enough.

choices.text: Give her the sign you practised

effects.log: You touch a sleeve, the way the sect taught its own, and she sees. She chooses the cure without a tremor. Nobody but you and the elder in the corner noticed.

choices.text: Trust her to do it alone

ok.log: She takes her time, smells every bowl twice and chooses right. The whole yard breathes again.

fail.log: She chooses wrong, and drinks the scorpion. The elders save her, as they always do, and send her home.

events.text: A year later a disciple in indigo with a centipede bracelet on one wrist walks into your camp without knocking. Ah Yao, of the Five Poisons Sect. She has brought you a cure for a cough you did not know you had, and news: she is going home for the New Rice festival.
events.arc: The Girl Who Wanted the Fifth Poison

choices.text: Go home with her for the festival

effects.log: Her grandmother sits you at the high end of the table. Ah Yao has made a cure for the old woman's knees, and the old woman pretends not to be proud.

choices.text: Ask her to show you what she learned

ok.log: She shows you the first form of the Scorpion Tail Hand, slowly, against a tree. You get it on the third try.

fail.log: She shows you too fast, and laughs at you, and shows you again. You are happy anyway.

choices.text: Wish her well and let her go

effects.log: She goes back up into the green mist with a wave. Years later you hear that she is an elder, and the best healer in the sect.

events.text: Ah Yao is back in her village after the failed trial, grinding roots for her grandmother. She will not talk about it. Then, one evening, she does: "The elders said I was too afraid. Was I?"
events.arc: The Girl Who Wanted the Fifth Poison

choices.text: Tell her fear is what makes a healer

effects.log: She thinks about that for a long time. The next year she is the one the villages send for when the fever comes.

choices.text: Help her train for next year

ok.log: A year of tubes, bites and bowls. At the next new moon she passes, and the first thing she does is send for you.

fail.log: A year of tubes and bites. She does not try the trial again, and is glad. You have both learned a great deal.

choices.text: Say you do not know

effects.log: "No," she agrees. "Nobody does." She goes back to her roots, and you sit with her until dark.

events.text: An old ginseng hunter shows you a root in the moss, no bigger than a finger, and ties a red thread round it before he digs. "Or it walks off in the night," he says, perfectly serious.

choices.text: Help him dig it out with a deer bone

ok.log: Root hair by root hair, for three hours. Not one breaks. He gives you a slice to chew, and the cold leaves your bones for a week.

fail.log: You break the tail of the root. The old man sighs and says it will still sell, but the mountain saw.

choices.text: Ask him why the thread is red

effects.log: He tells you a long story about a ginseng child who runs from greedy men. By the end you are tying threads yourself.

choices.text: Laugh at the thread

effects.log: He does not laugh back. That night your fire will not light, and he does not offer his.

events.text: The Liao River has frozen solid, and every child in the village is out on it with sledges, skates of bone and wooden tops whipped across the ice. A bigger child dares you to slide the whole way to the far bank.

choices.text: Take the dare

ok.log: You fly across the ice and crash into a snowbank on the far side, and the whole river cheers.

fail.log: You spin, fall, slide on your back the rest of the way and arrive anyway. They cheer louder for that.

choices.text: Whip a top with the little ones

effects.log: Your top spins longer than anyone's. A small girl declares you her best friend.

choices.text: Fish through a hole with the old men

effects.log: They teach you to sit still in the cold for an hour. You catch one fish, and are very proud.

events.text: The children of a Goryeo trader at the border market are kicking a shuttlecock of coins and feathers into the air, counting in their own tongue, and they let you into the circle.

choices.text: Try to beat their count

ok.log: Twenty kicks without a miss. They teach you to count to twenty in their language to celebrate.

fail.log: One kick, then the shuttlecock goes into a pot of soup. The trader laughs and gives you a bowl of it.

choices.text: Teach them a game from home

effects.log: They learn it in an afternoon and change all the rules. It is much better their way.

choices.text: Watch and count with them

effects.log: You count in two languages until the sun goes down behind the pines.

events.text: In the new snow behind the village there is a line of tiny paired prints going into the pines: a sable, the hunters say, the softest fur in the world. Nobody has caught one all winter.

choices.text: Follow the tracks into the forest

ok.log: At the end of the tracks, in a hollow log, a sable looks out at you, black-eyed and furious. You leave it be. You tell nobody where.

fail.log: The tracks go round and round, and so do you, until a hunter fetches you home by the ear.

choices.text: Set a snare the way the hunters do

effects.log: You catch nothing but a crow, which is cross about it. The hunters say you set it well.

choices.text: Draw the prints in the snow at home

effects.log: You draw them so well that an old hunter asks to keep the drawing in his head.

events.text: Snowed in at a farmhouse for three days, you sleep on the warm brick bed with the whole family, and the grandmother tells stories every night about the fox wives and tiger kings of the Long White Mountain.

choices.text: Listen to every story

effects.log: By the third night you know them all, and tell the last one back to her. She corrects only two things.

choices.text: Chop wood for the stove

effects.log: The family eats better for the wood, and so do you.

choices.text: Leave the moment the snow stops

effects.log: You go out into a world so white it hurts. The road is longer than you thought.

events.text: The wind on the snowfield has turned your fingers white and then grey, and you cannot feel your feet. Ahead there is a smudge of smoke, perhaps a camp, perhaps a long way off.

choices.text: Drive qi into your hands and walk

ok.log: Your hands burn back to life, then your feet. You reach the camp: Jurchen hunters, who give you broth and stare at your hands.

fail.log: You reach the camp, but your toes will ache in cold weather for the rest of your life.

choices.text: Dig into the snow and wait out the wind

effects.log: A snow hole is warmer than it has any right to be. You crawl out at dawn, cold and alive.

choices.text: Burn your pack to warm your hands

effects.log: You lose your spare clothes and 15 taels of goods to the fire. You keep your fingers.

events.text: Tiger tracks the size of rice bowls cross the road outside a hunting village. The tiger took a pony last week. The villagers have nailed a prayer to every door.

choices.text: Track the tiger to its den

ok.log: You meet it in a clearing. It looks at you a long time, and goes north into the deep forest, and does not come back. The village calls it a victory.

fail.log: It meets you before you meet it. You get away with a torn coat and four long scratches, and it gets away with its life.

choices.text: Help build a tiger fence of pine logs

effects.log: Five days of axes and frozen hands. The tiger looks at the fence, and goes round the village.

choices.text: Pray at the mountain god's shrine

effects.log: You leave a bowl of millet for the mountain. A week later the tracks stop. Who can say?

events.text: At the winter fur market of Liaoyang, Jurchen, Han and Goryeo traders shout prices across stacks of sable, fox and wolf. A young trapper is about to sell a black fox pelt for a tenth of what it is worth.

choices.text: Tell him what it is worth

effects.log: He gets three times the price and tries to give you half. You take a cup of tea instead.

choices.text: Buy it yourself and sell it on

ok.log: You buy cheap and sell dear to a Goryeo merchant who knows a good pelt. The trapper never finds out.

fail.log: The merchant you sell to knows exactly what you did, and pays you exactly what you paid.

choices.text: Buy a wolf-fur hat (20 taels)

effects.log: Warm, ugly and perfect. The wind stops mattering.

events.text: At the border post on the Yalu River, a Goryeo envoy and a Han customs officer have been shouting at each other for an hour, through an interpreter who is clearly getting it wrong on purpose.

choices.text: Translate for them honestly

ok.log: Enough of the words, the right way round. The envoy bows to you, the officer pours tea, and the interpreter leaves quickly.

fail.log: Your Goryeo is not as good as you thought. Both sides end up angry at you instead of each other, which is an improvement.

choices.text: Expose the interpreter

ok.log: He had been paid by a smuggler to keep the post shut. The officer has him marched off, and the gate opens.

fail.log: You cannot prove it. The interpreter smiles at you all afternoon.

choices.text: Wait for the gate to open

effects.log: It opens at dusk. You spend the day trading sour cabbage recipes with a Goryeo carter.

events.text: Jurchen hunters are hauling a great net under the ice of a frozen lake, horses turning a wooden wheel, men chopping holes in a long line. They are short of hands.

choices.text: Haul on the net with them

ok.log: The net comes up full of silver fish frozen solid the moment they touch the air. You eat with the hunters, and they teach you a song.

fail.log: You go through a hole up to your waist. They pull you out, laughing, and sit you by the fire.

choices.text: Chop holes along the line

effects.log: Hard work, and good. You are given your share of fish.

choices.text: Watch from the shore

effects.log: You watch the horses turn the wheel in the low sun until your eyelashes freeze.

events.text: A young soldier from the border garrison is hiding in a woodshed, half frozen, with no coat. He ran, he says, because the captain was selling the garrison's grain to smugglers and the men were starving.

choices.text: Give him your coat and send him home

effects.log: He goes south over the snow. You are cold for a week, and do not mind.

choices.text: Take his story to the garrison

ok.log: A general from Shenyang hears you out. The captain is in chains by spring, and the soldier is pardoned.

fail.log: The captain hears you out instead. You leave the garrison quickly, and the soldier leaves Liaodong.

choices.text: Turn him in for the reward

effects.log: The garrison pays you 25 taels. You do not ask what happens to him.

events.text: A man in a fine coat is selling "thousand-year ginseng" from a lacquered box in the market. The root has a beautiful shape. It also has, on close inspection, the marks of a carving knife.

choices.text: Inspect it closely

ok.log: Carved from a turnip root and soaked in tea. You say so, quietly, to the buyer. The man in the fine coat leaves by the back.

fail.log: It looks real enough to you. Luckily you could not afford it.

choices.text: Buy it as a curiosity (5 taels)

effects.log: He sells it to you for 5 taels, which tells you everything. It looks very fine on a shelf.

choices.text: Leave it to the buyers

effects.log: A family from the south buys it for their grandfather. You hope he never needs it.

events.text: High on the slopes of the Long White Mountain, where the snow never melts, a hot spring steams in a ring of black rocks. The local hunters say the mountain's breath comes up through it.

choices.text: Sit in the spring and cultivate

effects.log: Snow falling on your head, heat rising through your meridians. You come out with your qi like a clear stream.

choices.text: Climb on to the crater lake

ok.log: At the top, the lake of heaven lies in its crater like a blue eye. You stand there until your breath is part of the wind.

fail.log: The wind on the ridge turns you back. You go down slowly, beaten, and oddly happy.

choices.text: Leave an offering and go down

effects.log: A strip of red cloth on a branch, for the mountain. The hunters at the foot nod when they see you come down.

events.text: A trapper is lying in a snow hide on a ridge with a pigeon on a string, waiting for a white gyrfalcon, the bird the emperors pay for in silver. He has been waiting for nine days.

choices.text: Wait with him

ok.log: On the tenth day the falcon stoops out of the sun. The trapper catches it bare-handed and weeps. He insists you take a share of the price.

fail.log: Nothing comes. You learn to wait without moving, which is worth something.

choices.text: Bring down a pigeon for his bait

ok.log: One arrow, one pigeon. He nods at your bow with respect and tells you where the deer winter.

fail.log: You miss twice and scare off every bird on the ridge. He asks you, politely, to leave.

choices.text: Leave him to his patience

effects.log: You go down the ridge. Behind you he has not moved, and will not.

events.text: A blizzard comes down on the road into Liaodong with no warning at all, and through it you see a light: a hunters' cabin with a door that has a wolf's skull nailed over it.

choices.text: Knock and ask for shelter

effects.log: Three hunters let you in without a word, feed you, and talk about nothing but the snow all night. In the morning they show you the road.

choices.text: Shelter in the lee of the woodpile

ok.log: You sit out the storm wrapped in your own qi. When the hunters come out at dawn they stare, then laugh, then make you breakfast.

fail.log: The cold gets in. The hunters find you at dawn and carry you inside.

choices.text: Push on through the snow

effects.log: You arrive three days later than you should, and colder than you thought a person could be.

events.text: On the frozen Yalu, a Goryeo trader's sledge has gone through the ice at the edge and is sinking slowly, crates of paper and brass bowls sliding off the back. The trader is trying to hold it with a rope by himself.

choices.text: Take the rope and haul

ok.log: The sledge comes up with a crack of ice. The trader bows to you three times and gives you a brass bowl that rings like a bell.

fail.log: You save the trader and half the crates, and lose your boots to the river.

choices.text: Save the crates from the ice

effects.log: You carry crate after crate to the bank. The paper is dry and the trader is beside himself with thanks.

choices.text: Keep to the far side of the river

effects.log: Behind you, a sound of ice breaking, and a long silence.

events.text: After the winter hunt your sect eats together in the great log hall, as it has for two hundred years: the pack eats together, the riders say, or it does not eat. Tonight the sect head has put a junior at the high table, and the old riders are muttering.

choices.text: Sit beside the junior

effects.log: The muttering stops when you sit down. The junior eats like a starving pup, and never forgets who sat beside them.

choices.text: Tell the story of the hunt

ok.log: The hall roars at the end. The sect head raises a cup to you across the fire.

fail.log: Somebody else tells it better, with you as the one who fell off the horse. The hall roars anyway.

choices.text: Feed the wolves at the gate first

effects.log: The wolves eat when the pack eats. They know your smell now.

events.text: An old rider of your sect leads you out onto fresh snow and walks a circle without leaving a print. "Snow Wolf Steps," he says. "Your prints fill with snow before the hunters find them. Try."

choices.text: Learn the Snow Wolf Steps

ok.log: By the end of the week your prints are shallow; by the end of the month, gone. The old rider grunts.

fail.log: Your prints are deep and many. He makes you walk the circle until the moon comes up, and some of it sinks in.

choices.text: Ask about the riders who never came back

effects.log: He tells you their names, one by one, all afternoon. The sect remembers its dead.

choices.text: Run the ridge with him instead

effects.log: He is sixty and leaves you behind on the first slope. You are stronger for trying.

events.text: Your sect guards the ginseng roads for a price, and a poor hunters' village has not paid this season. The rider in charge wants an example made. The village headman is waiting in the snow with his hat in his hands.

choices.text: Waive the toll this year

effects.log: The rider in charge is not pleased. The village sends the sect its best root in the spring, unasked.

choices.text: Collect it, but gently

effects.log: The headman pays in furs. You leave him enough to get through the winter.

choices.text: Make the example

effects.log: You take the toll and the headman's horse. The roads are quiet, and the villages look away when the riders pass.

events.text: A man-eating tiger is on the ginseng roads, and your sect has sent riders out by twos to find it before the hunters lose their nerve. You and one other ride east under a white sky.

choices.text: Find it before your partner does

ok.log: Alone in a ravine, it and you. You ride home with its pelt across your saddle and the hunters cheering on the roads.

fail.log: It finds you first. Your partner drives it off, and the pack does not let you forget it.

choices.text: Hunt it as a pair, the pack's way

ok.log: Your partner drives it, you shoot. One arrow each, and the tiger lies still. You share the merit and the glory.

fail.log: You miss. Your partner does not. You ride home second, alive.

choices.text: Guard the hunters' camp instead

effects.log: The tiger never comes to the camp. The hunters sleep, for the first time in a week.

events.text: A rider in grey furs with a white wolf's tail on his sabre watches you bring down a running deer in the snow, then rides over. "The White Wolf Sect eats together," he says. "We are short of a seat at the table."

choices.text: Ride with him to the White Wolf Sect

effects.log: Up through the pines to a log hall on a ridge, wolves running beside the horses. That night you eat with the pack. You are a rider of the White Wolf Sect now.

choices.text: Ask what the pack does for silver

effects.log: "We guard the ginseng roads," he says, "for a price. Ask around." You do. The answers are mixed.

choices.text: Share the deer with him and decline

effects.log: He eats, nods, and rides off. "The seat stays empty a while," he calls back.

events.text: Old Jang Seok, a Goryeo-born ginseng hunter who has worked the Long White Mountain for fifty winters, says he has found it at last: a root a hundred years old, in a valley nobody else knows. He is too old to dig it alone and too proud to say so. "I need a pair of hands that can keep a secret," he says.

choices.text: Give him your hands and your word

effects.log: He looks at you for a long time and then nods. "We go at the first thaw."

choices.text: Ask for a share of the price

effects.log: "A third," he says, without blinking. "And your silence." You shake on it.

choices.text: Tell him he is too old for this

effects.log: He laughs until he coughs. "So is the root," he says, and goes alone. You never hear what became of him.

events.text: At the first thaw you go up into the mountain with Jang Seok. Three days in, you find tracks behind you: four men on horses, keeping their distance. Jang Seok knows the horses. They belong to Gao Shun, the fur baron of Liaoyang, who buys every root on the mountain at his own price.

choices.text: Lead the riders astray in the forest

ok.log: A false trail down a frozen stream. By nightfall the riders are lost in the wrong valley, and you and the old man are alone.

fail.log: They are not fooled for long, but long enough. You reach the valley a day ahead of them.

choices.text: Go back and face them on the trail

ok.log: Four riders, one narrow trail, one of you. They ride back down to Liaoyang with a message for their master.

fail.log: They knock you into a snowdrift and ride on. But the old man has slipped away into the forest, and you catch up with him at dusk.

events.text: In the hidden valley, under a pine older than the empire, the root is everything Jang Seok said, its red berries bright in the snow. You are three hours into the digging when the blizzard comes over the ridge, and with it, torches: Gao Shun himself, with ten men. "A hundred taels for the root," he calls down, "and you both walk home."

choices.text: Finish the dig and run for it

ok.log: The last root hair comes free. You carry the old man on your back down a ravine the horses cannot follow, and the snow fills in your tracks.

fail.log: You get the root and the old man out, but not cleanly: you fall the last stretch of the ravine and limp for a month.

choices.text: Stand and fight for it

ok.log: Gao Shun's men break in the blizzard. The baron himself goes down the mountain on foot, without his horse or his torch.

fail.log: You are beaten down in the snow, but the old man has the root inside his coat and is gone into the white. They do not find him.

choices.text: Sell him the root

effects.log: Gao Shun pays 100 taels into your hand. Jang Seok sits down in the snow and does not get up for a long time.

events.text: Back in the village, Jang Seok holds the root up in the lamplight. Half the families on the mountain are sick with the winter cough, and a merchant from the capital has already offered a fortune for the root. The old man looks at you. "You carried it," he says. "You choose."

choices.text: Brew it for the sick villages

effects.log: Slice by slice, the root goes into a hundred pots. The cough leaves the mountain. In every village they tie a red thread on their door for you.

choices.text: Sell it and share the fortune

effects.log: The capital merchant pays a fortune. Your share is 150 taels, and Jang Seok builds a house of real stone for his old age.

choices.text: Keep a slice for yourself

ok.log: The rest goes to the sick. The slice you chew burns through your meridians like a summer sun. You feel years come back to you.

fail.log: The rest goes to the sick. The slice is too strong for you and you lie in a fever for three days, but you rise stronger.

events.text: The winter after you sold the root, the cough comes to the mountain and there is no great root left to stop it. Jang Seok is among the sick. When you go to his door, his grandson answers, and does not open it all the way.

choices.text: Bring every root you can buy (60 taels)

effects.log: You spend 60 taels on lesser roots and carry them up through the snow. The old man lives through the winter. He never says your name again.

choices.text: Go to Gao Shun and demand the root back

ok.log: He has not sold it yet. You shame him in front of his whole household, and he sends a slice up the mountain. It is enough.

fail.log: He has you thrown out of his house in Liaoyang. On the mountain, the cough runs its course.

choices.text: Leave Liaodong for the south

effects.log: You go south past the wall into the northern plains. The snow behind you is very white and very quiet.

events.text: At the border market on the Yalu, Captain Lu Ke of the customs post has arrested Yun Seolhwa, a Goryeo paper merchant whose family has traded at this market for three generations, for smuggling. Her clerk is in tears in the street, holding the family ledger. "It is all here," he says, "every tael. Nobody will read it."

choices.text: Read the ledger

ok.log: Every crate, every tax, every seal. It is clean. But one page shows the captain's own seal on goods that never came through.

fail.log: Half of it is in Goryeo script. The clerk reads it to you through the night, and you understand enough.

choices.text: Ask around the market

effects.log: Everyone has a story about Captain Lu Ke, and none of them is good. Nobody will say it to his face.

choices.text: Keep out of a border quarrel

effects.log: Foreign merchants and imperial officers: not a thing a traveller should touch. You walk on.

events.text: The clerk takes you to a warehouse by the river at night. Inside are crates with Captain Lu Ke's seal on them: furs and ginseng going over the river untaxed, under Yun Seolhwa's family name. Then there are lanterns at the door.

choices.text: Fight your way out with the proof

ok.log: You go out through the river door with a sealed bill of lading inside your coat and two guards in the water behind you.

fail.log: You get out, and the clerk gets out with the bill of lading, but you have a guard's staff across your ribs to remember it by.

choices.text: Hide among the crates

ok.log: The guards count the crates and leave. You hear them name the captain twice. You have heard enough.

fail.log: They find the clerk. You get him out over the roof, but without the papers. All you have is what you heard.

events.text: A censor from Shenyang has come to judge Yun Seolhwa's case in the customs hall. Captain Lu Ke stands beside him, very calm. Before the hearing, the captain finds you in the yard and offers you a post as his deputy, "for a sensible person who knows when to forget a warehouse."

choices.text: Lay the proof before the censor

ok.log: The censor reads the bill of lading twice, then looks at the captain for a long time. Yun Seolhwa walks out of the hall free, and Lu Ke does not.

fail.log: The censor believes you, but cannot prove it in one day. He frees Yun Seolhwa and sends the captain to a post in the far north.

choices.text: Have Yun Seolhwa's ledger read aloud

effects.log: Three hours of numbers in a cold hall. By the end of it, the whole room has understood, and the censor has too.

choices.text: Take the captain's offer

effects.log: You say nothing at the hearing. Yun Seolhwa is fined into ruin and sent back over the river. Your new post pays well.

events.text: In the spring Yun Seolhwa's carts come back over the Yalu, loaded with the finest mulberry paper in the world. She sends for you and bows, a long Goryeo bow, then hands you a book of blank pages bound in blue silk. "For your own ledger," she says. "Keep it as clean as mine."

choices.text: Accept the book

effects.log: You write in it for the rest of your life. Every merchant at the border knows your name, and gives you a fair price.

choices.text: Ask her to teach you the border trade

effects.log: She teaches you paper, ginseng and brass, and which officers are honest. You make 40 taels the first season.

choices.text: Ask only for a cup of barley tea

effects.log: She laughs and pours it. You drink it in her warehouse, among the paper, while snow falls on the river.

events.text: A year as Captain Lu Ke's deputy. The silver is good and the nights are long. Then a new censor arrives from the capital, with a copy of a ledger in Goryeo script that someone sent him from across the river.

choices.text: Confess everything to the censor

effects.log: You lose your post and your savings in fines, but not your head. The captain loses both posts and a great deal more.

choices.text: Burn the warehouse records

ok.log: The records burn, the case falls, and the censor goes home angry. You keep your post, and you do not sleep well.

fail.log: You are seen. You leave the border post that night with nothing, and the captain hangs the blame on you.

choices.text: Flee south before the hearing

effects.log: You ride south past the great wall with your silver and your name, and only one of them is worth anything now.

events.text: On a ginseng road a hunters' village shows you its toll receipts. They pay the White Wolf Sect for protection every season, like everyone. This year they have paid twice: once to the sect, and once to a rider named Han Bo, who wears the sect's grey furs and says the price has gone up.

choices.text: Look into Han Bo

effects.log: You ask on the roads. Three villages have paid him twice. The sect, it seems, knows nothing.

choices.text: Pay the village's second toll back (20 taels)

effects.log: You give the headman 20 taels. He takes it, and tells you everything about Han Bo.

choices.text: Stay out of the pack's business

effects.log: Wolves settle their own quarrels. You go on along the road.

events.text: You find Han Bo at a roadhouse with a stack of silver in front of him and a white wolf's tail on his sabre. He is not ashamed. "The sect takes the roads' silver and eats it in the great hall," he says. "I take a little more and give it to my mother. Who is the thief?"

choices.text: Ask about his mother

effects.log: She is real, and sick, and lives in a hut below the ridge. The sect never asked. Han Bo never told them.

choices.text: Call him a thief to his face

ok.log: His sabre is quick, yours is quicker. He sits down hard among his silver and listens to you after that.

fail.log: He knocks you over a bench and walks out with the silver. But he walks slowly, and looks back.

events.text: The White Wolf Sect has heard. A party of riders is coming down the ridge to take Han Bo back to the great hall, where the pack judges its own. Han Bo is saddling his horse to run. He looks at you. "Well?" he says.

choices.text: Speak for him before the pack

effects.log: You stand in the great hall as one of the pack and tell them about the hut below the ridge. The sect head listens. Then the sect sends a healer to Han Bo's mother.

choices.text: Ride with him to face the pack

ok.log: You tell the riders about the hut below the ridge. They are quiet a long time. They take Han Bo back, and they send a healer with him.

fail.log: The riders do not listen to an outsider. They take Han Bo to the hall. But they look at the hut as they pass it.

choices.text: Help him run

ok.log: Through the pines, over the frozen river, gone. The White Wolf Sect does not forget a face that helped a wolf run.

fail.log: The riders catch you both at the river. Han Bo goes back to the hall, and you go back with a long cold walk and a pack that knows your face.

choices.text: Let the pack take him

effects.log: You step aside. The riders nod to you as they pass. Han Bo does not look at you.

events.text: The pack has judged Han Bo. He paid back every village twice over and gave up his sabre for a season. Now he is a rider again, and he has come to find you on the road, with a white wolf's tail in his hand.

choices.text: Accept the tail

effects.log: A white wolf's tail is the pack's thanks. Riders on the ginseng roads nod to you for the rest of your life, and the hunters' villages remember.

choices.text: Ask him to teach you the sabre

ok.log: He teaches you the first form of the Howling Sabre in the snow, over and over, until the snow comes off your blade like his.

fail.log: He teaches you, and you are slow, and he is patient for the first time in his life. It is a good winter.

choices.text: Ask after his mother

effects.log: She is well. She has knitted you a pair of mittens out of wolf wool. They are hideous and very warm.

events.text: Two winters after Han Bo ran, the White Wolf Sect's riders find you on a ginseng road. They do not draw their sabres. They only ride beside you, close, for a whole day, and then the leader says: "The pack eats together. You chose to feed one wolf alone."

choices.text: Tell them about his mother

ok.log: The leader is quiet for a long time. Then he rides away, and the pack lets the matter go.

fail.log: They have heard it before. They take your horse as the toll, and ride off.

choices.text: Pay the pack's fine (40 taels)

effects.log: The leader weighs the 40 taels in his hand, nods, and rides off. The roads are open to you again.

choices.text: Stare them down

ok.log: Nobody moves. At dusk they turn and ride for the ridge, and the roads talk about it all winter.

fail.log: The pack teaches you why it is a pack. You limp to the next village.

events.text: At the Red Gate at the foot of Mount Tai the stairway begins: six thousand steps, and pilgrims of every kind on them, from a governor in a sedan chair to a barefoot widow with a bundle of incense.

choices.text: Climb with the pilgrims

effects.log: You climb all day among strangers who share their water and their bad knees. At the top nobody is a stranger.

choices.text: Carry a pilgrim's bundle for coins

effects.log: A merchant's wife pays you to carry her offerings to the Middle Gate. Your shoulders will remember her.

choices.text: Watch them from the gate

effects.log: You sit under the old cypress and watch the stairway fill and empty like a river. It is a lesson of its own.

events.text: Below the mountain the incense market never closes. Sellers shout over each other: prayer slips, paper horses, stone tablets carved with your name while you wait.

choices.text: Buy a prayer slip (5 taels)

effects.log: You write a wish you will not tell anyone and tie it to the pine at the Middle Gate.

choices.text: Haggle for the fun of it

ok.log: The seller laughs, gives up, and throws in a paper horse. You leave with more than you paid for.

fail.log: The seller has been haggling since before you were born. You pay full price and are thanked for it.

choices.text: Walk through without buying

effects.log: Heaven, you decide, does not keep accounts in paper horses.

events.text: In Qufu, in the shade of the old master's temple, a village schoolteacher is reading the classics aloud to anyone who will sit. Most of his listeners are asleep.

choices.text: Sit and listen

effects.log: You stay awake for all of it. On the road afterwards one line keeps coming back, about learning and never tiring.

choices.text: Argue a passage with him

ok.log: He argues back with delight. By evening half the sleepers are awake and taking sides.

fail.log: He corrects you so gently you do not notice until the next day, when you blush on the road.

choices.text: Leave a little silver for the school (10 taels)

effects.log: He bows over the coins as if you had given him a book.

events.text: At a temple fair in Taian the young men of the villages are lifting the stone lions from the gate, one by one, while their grandmothers judge.

choices.text: Lift a lion

ok.log: The lion comes off its plinth and the grandmothers nod as one. It is the best praise in Shandong.

fail.log: The lion stays where it is and your back says something rude about it for a week.

choices.text: Just cheer the others

effects.log: You cheer a farmer's boy who lifts his lion an inch, and he grins at you all the way home.

choices.text: Buy fried dough sticks for the judges (4 taels)

effects.log: The grandmothers accept them as a bribe, and judge everyone more kindly for an hour.

events.text: The Grand Canal runs through western Shandong, slow and brown, and the grain barges crawl up it toward the capital pulled by teams of trackers singing a hauling song.

choices.text: Take a turn on the tow rope

effects.log: By the third song you know the words. By the fifth your hands do. The trackers share their millet with you.

choices.text: Ride a barge north (10 taels)

effects.log: You sleep on a sack of grain and wake to the hauling song. It is the slowest, sweetest journey.

choices.text: Ask the bargemen the news

effects.log: They know who is rich in the capital and who is hungry in the villages, and they think it is the same story.

events.text: In a market town at the edge of the reed marshes everyone is talking quietly about the marsh outlaws: who they robbed, who they fed, and who has gone into the reeds to join them.

choices.text: Ask who they rob

effects.log: Tax collectors, grain hoarders, a magistrate's cousin. Never the fishermen, they say, and look at you to see if you believe it.

choices.text: Warn the town against them

effects.log: The townsfolk thank you politely and talk about something else until you leave.

choices.text: Keep your ears open and your mouth shut

effects.log: You learn the names of three reed channels and the hour the patrol boats sleep.

events.text: A widow who sells pancakes rolled with scallion at the foot of the mountain has been robbed by her own landlord, who raised the rent on her stall three times this year.

choices.text: Speak to the landlord for her

ok.log: The landlord finds that he had always meant to lower the rent. The widow gives you pancakes for a month.

fail.log: The landlord finds you rude. The widow finds you kind, which is something.

choices.text: Pay a season of her rent (30 taels)

effects.log: She counts it twice and cries once. The next morning her stall has a new awning.

choices.text: Buy a pancake and move on

effects.log: Scallion, sesame and a sad smile. It is the best pancake on the mountain.

events.text: Just before dawn on the summit the pilgrims wrapped in rented quilts fall silent all at once, and below them the sea of clouds turns gold.

choices.text: Breathe with the sunrise

effects.log: Your breath goes out over the clouds and comes back warm. Something in your meridians settles into place.

choices.text: Look for the emperors' stone

effects.log: You find the great blank stele that some old emperor left without a word on it. You understand him a little.

choices.text: Sleep through it

effects.log: You wake to the pilgrims coming down, all smiling at something you missed. Next time.

events.text: A shrine on the lower slope cracked in last spring's tremor. The keeper, an old woman with a broom, says the mountain shrugged, and it is not her place to argue with it.

choices.text: Help her mend the wall

effects.log: Two days of mortar and stone. When it is done she gives you a cup of tea so strong it is nearly a technique.

choices.text: Give silver for the mending (15 taels)

effects.log: She takes it with both hands and writes your name on the donors' board in a very small hand.

choices.text: Ask her about the mountain

effects.log: She talks for an hour about the mountain as if it were a stubborn husband. You learn more than you expect.

events.text: The village children of Taian keep fighting crickets in clay pots, and one of them has challenged you, very seriously, to bring a cricket of your own.

choices.text: Catch one in the fields

ok.log: Your cricket is small and furious and wins twice. You are famous among everyone under the age of ten.

fail.log: Your cricket hops out of the pot and away into the grass. Everyone agrees it was the cleverest cricket.

choices.text: Be the judge instead

effects.log: You judge so fairly that two of the losers thank you. You will be a magistrate one day, they decide.

choices.text: Set all the crickets free

effects.log: There is a great deal of shouting. Later, in the quiet, the fields sing.

events.text: Your neighbours are taking the whole street up Mount Tai for the spring festival, and somebody has to carry the smallest one when the steps get steep.

choices.text: Carry the little one

effects.log: You carry the child up the Eighteen Bends, counting steps out loud together. You reach the top with legs of jelly.

choices.text: Race the other children up

ok.log: You reach the South Gate of Heaven first and stand there shouting down at the others. A monk laughs.

fail.log: You slip on the dewy steps and arrive last, with a scraped knee and a story.

choices.text: Stay with the grandmothers

effects.log: You climb slowly with the grandmothers, who tell you which pine was planted by which emperor.

events.text: A fisherman's son is teaching you to pole a little flat boat through the reed channels, and swears the marsh outlaws live just past the next bend.

choices.text: Pole to the next bend

effects.log: Past the bend there is only more reed and a heron. You both decide the outlaws saw you coming and hid.

choices.text: Pretend to be the outlaws

effects.log: You spend the afternoon robbing frogs of their lily pads. You are terrible outlaws and very happy ones.

choices.text: Go home before dark

effects.log: You are home before the lamps are lit, and nobody has to come looking. That night you dream of reeds.

events.text: On the pilgrims' road up from Taian, three men in borrowed monks' robes are stopping pilgrims and selling "blessings" with knives under their sleeves.

choices.text: Throw them off the mountain road

ok.log: The false monks run down the steps faster than they ever climbed them. The pilgrims cheer you to the next shrine.

fail.log: One of them knows how to use the knife. You drive them off, but you bleed for the honour.

choices.text: Shame them in front of the pilgrims

ok.log: You ask them to recite one sutra. They cannot. The pilgrims do the rest, with walking sticks.

fail.log: They recite a very convincing sutra. You are not sure any more, and neither are the pilgrims.

choices.text: Climb past them

effects.log: You walk on. Behind you a pilgrim pays for a blessing.

events.text: Where the road crosses the reed country a magistrate's patrol boat is stopping every traveller, looking for the marsh outlaws, and looking very hard at your hands for calluses.

choices.text: Answer their questions calmly

ok.log: The sergeant decides you are a scholar of some sort and waves you on with an apology.

fail.log: They keep you on the bank until dusk and take a "crossing fee" for their trouble.

choices.text: Pay the crossing fee (10 taels)

effects.log: The sergeant pockets it without writing anything down. The reeds rustle as you cross.

choices.text: Slip across by the reed channels

ok.log: You cross on the reed tops like a heron. On the far side a fisherman nods to you, as if you had passed a test.

fail.log: You land in the mud to your waist, in full view of the patrol. They laugh too hard to arrest you.

events.text: Your sect drills on the stone terrace above the sea of clouds every dawn. Elder Shi Bai walks the lines and pushes each disciple on the shoulder. Whoever moves, starts again.

choices.text: Stand like the mountain

ok.log: His hand pushes and nothing happens. He grunts, which from Elder Shi is a poem. Your stance roots a little deeper.

fail.log: You rock one step back and start again from the first form. And again. By noon you have learned a great deal about stone.

choices.text: Watch how the senior disciples stand

effects.log: Their weight is in the earth, not in the legs. You see it for the first time.

choices.text: Meditate on the cliff edge after

effects.log: The wind comes up from the valley and goes round you. You let it.

events.text: An imperial envoy has come up the mountain to prepare the rites, and your sect is told to stand guard on the summit in clean robes and keep the curious away.

choices.text: Guard the rites with the others

effects.log: You stand all day and all night beside the altar. The envoy notices nothing. The elders notice everything.

choices.text: Turn away a noble who pushes in

ok.log: His bodyguard tries you and sits down on the steps, surprised. The envoy thanks your sect in his report.

fail.log: The bodyguard is better than he looks. Elder Shi steps in and ends it, and says nothing to you, which is worse.

choices.text: Look at the old carved stones while you stand

effects.log: Between the hours you read the cliffs: poems of emperors, a thousand years of them.

events.text: In the pine wood below the Jade Emperor's summit the oldest disciple of your sect teaches the Pine Sword to anyone who will stand in the wind long enough to learn it.

choices.text: Stand in the wind and learn

effects.log: You stand until your arms forget they are arms. Then the sword moves the way the pine does: holding, never fighting.

choices.text: Spar with her instead

ok.log: You touch her sleeve once. She laughs and bows, and tells the elders you have the root of it.

fail.log: She taps your wrist, your shoulder and your forehead with a pine twig. You thank her.

choices.text: Gather pine resin for the infirmary

effects.log: Sticky work, but the infirmary keeper writes your name in the merit book.

events.text: Word comes up the mountain that the marsh outlaws have robbed a tax barge. The elders of your sect argue about whether the mountain should come down into the reeds.

choices.text: Speak for leaving the outlaws alone

effects.log: "They rob the robbers," you say. Half the hall agrees. Elder Shi says the mountain does not take sides with water.

choices.text: Volunteer to hunt them

effects.log: You go down with five disciples and come back with nothing but mud and a respect for reeds.

choices.text: Keep silent and listen

effects.log: You learn more about the elders from this one argument than from a year of lessons.

events.text: At the South Gate of Heaven a disciple of the Taishan Sect in brown and gold watches the pilgrims come up the last steps. "You climb like someone who wants to stand somewhere," she says. "The mountain has room."

choices.text: Ask to join the Taishan Sect

effects.log: She walks you to the hall and the elders test you by pushing on your shoulders. You do not move. You are one of them.

choices.text: Ask what the sect stands for

effects.log: "Stand like the mountain," she says, "unmoved, and in the open." You think about it all the way down.

choices.text: Thank her and climb on

effects.log: She bows. The gate stays open behind you, as the mountain does.

events.text: At the Red Gate an old woman named Kang Lianer, bent nearly double, asks if you will walk with her to the summit. She carries a prayer slip her husband wrote forty years ago and never had the strength to take up the mountain.

choices.text: Walk with her

effects.log: She takes your arm as if she had always known you. The first thousand steps go by in stories about him.

choices.text: Hire her a sedan chair (20 taels)

effects.log: "He climbed nothing in a chair," she says, but she lets you pay, and walks beside it.

choices.text: Wish her well and climb ahead

effects.log: She waves you on. You see her bundle far below you all day, never stopping.

events.text: At the Middle Gate of Heaven a storm comes up the mountain. Kang Lianer will not shelter: thieves are working the crowded shelters, she says, and her husband's slip is all she has. Two of them are already watching her bundle.

choices.text: Face down the thieves

ok.log: They decide the bundle is not worth it. Kang Lianer thanks you by giving you half her steamed bun.

fail.log: They get your purse instead of her bundle. She says it was a fair trade, and means it.

choices.text: Shelter her with your own coat

effects.log: You climb on through the rain together with your coat over her and the slip. You are soaked; it is dry.

choices.text: Talk her into the shelter

ok.log: She sits between you and the wall all night with the slip in her sleeve, and the thieves move on.

fail.log: She will not be talked into anything. You climb on in the rain behind her.

events.text: On the Eighteen Bends, the steepest stretch, Kang Lianer's legs give out. She sits on a step below the South Gate of Heaven, a few hundred steps from the top, and says quietly that this is far enough, and that you should take the slip up.

choices.text: Carry her the rest of the way

ok.log: You carry her up on your back, step by step, with half the pilgrims on the bends cheering you on.

fail.log: Your legs fail a hundred steps short. Two porters take her the rest of the way, and you crawl after.

choices.text: Lend her your qi

ok.log: Your palm on her back, your breath with hers. She stands, astonished, and climbs the last bends on her own feet.

fail.log: Your qi goes into her like water into sand, and she still cannot stand. You carry her after all, slowly.

choices.text: Take the slip up for her

effects.log: You climb alone with the slip in your sleeve and burn it on the summit. When you come down she is asleep on the step, smiling.

events.text: Dawn on the summit. Kang Lianer stands at the edge above the sea of clouds and reads her husband's slip aloud before she burns it. It is a love poem, and a bad one. Every pilgrim on the summit is crying.

choices.text: Bow to the sunrise with her

effects.log: She holds your hand while the sun comes up. "He would have liked you," she says. You carry that down the mountain.

choices.text: Write a slip of your own

effects.log: You burn a slip beside hers. You never tell anyone what was on it. The sunrise is very bright.

events.text: Years later a young man in a carter's coat finds you and asks if you are the one who took his grandmother up Mount Tai. She talked about it until the end, he says, and she wanted you to have the thing she kept.

choices.text: Accept her keepsake

effects.log: It is a little wooden pilgrim's token, worn smooth by her thumb. It goes everywhere with you after.

choices.text: Ask him to keep it for his children

effects.log: He nods slowly and puts it back in his coat. "Then they will hear about you," he says.

events.text: A letter finds you, years after the mountain, in a careful hand that is not hers: Kang Lianer has gone to join her husband, and asks that the one who carried her slip be told that she dreamt of the summit every night after.

choices.text: Light incense for her

effects.log: You light it facing east, toward a mountain you cannot see from here. The smoke goes straight up.

choices.text: Climb the mountain again for her

effects.log: You climb the six thousand steps alone, and on the summit you read the letter aloud to nobody.

events.text: Poling through the reed marshes, your boat is boarded by a dozen men and women with fish spears. Their chief, a long quiet man they call Iron Heron Qiao Ming, asks who you work for. Behind him a grey-haired woman, Mother Fen, holds a ledger.

choices.text: Tell him the truth: nobody

effects.log: Qiao Ming studies you a long time, then gives you fish soup and a place by the fire.

choices.text: Fight your way free

ok.log: Three spears go into the water. Qiao Ming lifts his hands, smiling. "Good," he says. "Eat with us."

fail.log: The reeds are their country, not yours. You wake on a mud bank with your purse lighter and a bowl of soup beside you.

choices.text: Pay them to let you pass (20 taels)

effects.log: Mother Fen writes it in her ledger, "a toll, from a polite one," and they let you go.

events.text: Mother Fen shows you the ledger by lamplight. Every tael the band takes from the magistrate's grain barges is written down, and every sack they give back to the starving villages along the canal. "Someone should see it," she says.

choices.text: Read it with her

effects.log: Page after page, in a careful hand. Robbery, yes. Also more bread than the magistrate has given out in ten years.

choices.text: Help them hand out grain

effects.log: You spend a night poling sacks to a village where the children are too thin to cheer. They cheer anyway.

choices.text: Leave the marsh at dawn

effects.log: Qiao Ming lets you go with a nod. "The reeds remember," he says.

events.text: In the town on the marsh's edge, Magistrate Wei Tong sends for you. He has heard you know the reed channels. He offers 300 taels for the hour the band gathers, and the threat of a cell if you refuse.

choices.text: Take his offer

effects.log: He smiles and pours tea. "The hour and the channel," he says. You give them.

choices.text: Refuse him to his face

ok.log: Something in your voice makes him decide you are not worth the trouble. You walk out free and he watches you go.

fail.log: He gives you a month in the cells to think about it. You come out thinner, and still saying no.

choices.text: Pretend to agree and warn the band

ok.log: You give him a channel that goes nowhere and pole out that night to Qiao Ming with the true hour of the raid.

fail.log: He has you followed. You lose the tail in the reeds, but the magistrate knows now which side you are on.

events.text: The night of the raid. The magistrate's war boats come into the reeds with torches, and the Reedwater Band is waiting for them in the dark, because you told them. Qiao Ming hands you a fish spear. "Stand with us," he says.

choices.text: Fight in the reeds beside them

ok.log: The war boats turn and flee with their torches hissing in the water. At dawn the villages of the marsh know your name.

fail.log: A spear takes you in the side. Mother Fen sews you up by lamplight, scolding, and the band wins without you.

choices.text: Burn the empty boats and spare the soldiers

effects.log: The soldiers swim home in the dark with nothing to show the magistrate but their wet sleeves. Nobody dies in the reeds tonight.

choices.text: Slip away before it starts

effects.log: You hear it behind you all night, the shouting in the reeds. In the morning you are three towns away.
