events.text: The reeds burn for two nights. The magistrate's men bring out bodies under sacking, and the band's ledger, and Mother Fen in a cage. Wei Tong pays you 300 taels in front of the whole town, so that the whole town will remember.

choices.text: Keep the silver

effects.log: You keep it. In the market nobody will sell to you, and a child throws a reed at you and runs.

choices.text: Buy Mother Fen out of the cage

ok.log: The jailer takes the magistrate's silver from your hands and looks away one night. Mother Fen goes into the reeds without a word to you.

fail.log: The jailer takes the silver and reports you. You leave the province with nothing but your skin.

events.text: A year later a boy in a reed hat brings you a basket of dried fish and a folded page torn from Mother Fen's ledger. Your name is on it, under a line that reads only: "Said no to Wei Tong."

choices.text: Keep the page

effects.log: You fold it small and keep it with your things. Some debts are paid in fish.

choices.text: Send the boy back with silver for the villages (30 taels)

effects.log: He grins and runs. In the villages of the marsh, the next winter is a little less hungry.

events.text: On the cliffs at Penglai a fisher girl named Lan Qiu points out to sea, where a mirage has lifted towers and green islands above the water. "The isles of the immortals," she says. "I am going there."

choices.text: Watch the mirage with her

effects.log: For an hour there are palaces in the sea. Then there is only sea. Lan Qiu does not stop looking.

choices.text: Tell her it is only light on the water

effects.log: "So is the moon," she says, and keeps looking.

choices.text: Leave her to her dreaming

effects.log: You walk on along the cliffs. Behind you she is still pointing.

events.text: Lan Qiu has found a boatman, a smooth man called Master Huo, who sells passage to the immortal isles for everything a fishing family owns. Her mother has sold the nets. The boat leaves at the new moon.

choices.text: Look into Master Huo

ok.log: Three families have sailed with him. None came back, and none of their nets were ever sold twice. He is a swindler.

fail.log: Everyone says he is a fine man. You do not believe them, but you cannot say why.

choices.text: Go with her to see the boat

effects.log: It is a good boat, too good for the money. You stay close to her after that.

choices.text: Stay out of it

effects.log: It is her dream and her family's nets. You stay out of it, and it sits badly with you.

events.text: The new moon. Master Huo's boat is at the jetty, and Lan Qiu is on it with her bundle. Out past the harbour a storm is building where the mirage was, and Master Huo is already cutting the rope.

choices.text: Expose him on the jetty

ok.log: You name the three families aloud. The fishermen on the jetty take hold of Master Huo, and Lan Qiu climbs back onto land.

fail.log: He shouts you down and the boat goes out. You leap aboard after it.

choices.text: Leap onto the boat after her

effects.log: You land on the deck as the boat leaves the jetty. Master Huo looks at you the way a fox looks at a dog.

choices.text: Let the boat go

effects.log: The boat goes out into the dark. You watch until the storm takes the lamp.

events.text: Out at sea the storm hits. Master Huo is lowering the only small boat for himself. Lan Qiu is clinging to the mast, and the islands of the mirage are nowhere at all.

choices.text: Fight Master Huo for the small boat

ok.log: You put him in the bottom of the boat and row Lan Qiu home through the storm yourself. You come ashore at dawn.

fail.log: He gets away in the small boat. You and Lan Qiu ride the wreck to shore, half drowned, alive.

choices.text: Swim for shore with her

ok.log: You swim all night with her on your back. In the morning fishermen pull you both out of the surf.

fail.log: The sea is stronger than you. A fishing boat finds you clinging to a spar, and Lan Qiu beside you.

events.text: Lan Qiu mends nets on the cliff again. Master Huo is in the magistrate's cells, and the three families have been told what happened to theirs. She still looks at the sea, sometimes, when the mirage comes.

choices.text: Ask if she still believes in the isles

effects.log: "Of course," she says. "I am just going to swim there on my own, when I am better at it." You laugh together.

choices.text: Teach her to breathe the way you do

effects.log: She learns fast. Years later a fisherwoman of Penglai is known up and down the coast for diving deeper than anyone.

events.text: In Jining on the Grand Canal an old stone mason, Yan Shoucheng, is carving a memorial stele for a flood that drowned his street. The salt merchant Gou Ping, who paid for it, wants his own name at the top in larger characters than the dead.

choices.text: Help Yan with the heavy stone

effects.log: You lift the blank stele onto its turtle for him. He thanks you with a nod, the mason's way.

choices.text: Ask whose names go on it

effects.log: Forty-one names. Yan knows the faces of all of them. He tells you about six before he stops.

choices.text: Watch the canal go by

effects.log: You let the old man work. The barges go by. Nobody asks you anything.

events.text: Gou Ping comes to the yard with two guards and the new text: his name, his titles, his generosity, and the drowned in small letters at the bottom. Yan Shoucheng has put down his chisel and is not picking it up.

choices.text: Stand beside Yan

ok.log: The guards try to move you and find out what a mountain is. Gou Ping leaves, promising trouble.

fail.log: They knock you into the stone dust. Yan helps you up and says, "Thank you," and means it.

choices.text: Persuade Gou Ping that small names shame the giver

ok.log: He thinks about it, and about the gossip in the tea houses. He takes his name off the top, sourly.

fail.log: He tells you to mind your own stones. Yan picks up his chisel, very slowly, and carves nothing.

choices.text: Tell Yan to take the money

effects.log: "I have carved lies before," he says. "I am too old for another." He sends you away.

events.text: The night before the stele is raised, someone tries to break it with a hammer. You catch Gou Ping's steward at it in the yard, and behind him, in the dark, a carriage waiting.

choices.text: Drag the steward to the magistrate

effects.log: The steward talks to save himself. Gou Ping pays a fine and the town hears why. The stele goes up whole.

choices.text: Let him go, but carve his master's deed on the back

ok.log: You and Yan carve four plain lines on the back of the stele, and the whole canal comes to read them. Gou Ping leaves Jining.

fail.log: Your lines come out stiff and Yan chisels them off again, laughing. The stele goes up plain, and whole.

choices.text: Guard the stele until dawn

effects.log: You sit beside it all night. The carriage leaves. At dawn the town raises it with ropes and a song.

events.text: Years later, passing through Jining, you find the stele by the canal with fresh incense in front of it. At the bottom, in very small characters beneath the forty-one, someone has carved the name of the mason, and yours.

choices.text: Light a stick of incense

effects.log: The smoke goes up past forty-one names and two more. A barge goes by, singing.

choices.text: Find Yan Shoucheng's grave

effects.log: It is a plain stone he carved himself, with one word on it: "Mason." You leave a chisel on it.

events.text: Pilgrims climb Wudang Mountain all year to the Golden Summit, where a hall of gilded bronze sits on the highest peak and catches the lightning in summer without ever burning.

choices.text: Climb to the bronze hall

effects.log: At the top a storm breaks around the summit, and the bronze hall glows like a lamp. You come down very quiet.

choices.text: Make an offering at the hall (10 taels)

effects.log: A Taoist strikes the bell once for you. The sound goes out over the seventy-two peaks.

choices.text: Ask the Taoists about the lightning

effects.log: "Heaven touches the mountain and the mountain does not resist," says one. "So nothing breaks."

events.text: On the lakes east of Wuhan the lotus root harvest has begun. Families wade waist-deep in the cold mud, feeling for the long white roots with their feet.

choices.text: Wade in and help

effects.log: By evening you can find a root with your toes. The family feeds you lotus soup with pork ribs, and it is very good.

choices.text: Buy a basket of roots (5 taels)

effects.log: Crisp and sweet, with holes like a flute. You eat them on the road for days.

choices.text: Watch from the dike

effects.log: The pickers sing as they wade, a slow song that goes with the mud. You learn it without meaning to.

events.text: From the Yellow Crane Tower above Wuchang the great river looks wide enough to be a sea. Poets have written on the walls for a thousand years, and a young one is staring at a blank space, afraid to fill it.

choices.text: Write a line beside the old poems

ok.log: You write four lines about the river and the crane that never came back. People copy them before the ink is dry.

fail.log: You write four lines. The young poet reads them politely and then, encouraged, writes eight better ones.

choices.text: Encourage the young poet

effects.log: She writes, slowly, and it is good. She bows to you as if you had written it yourself.

choices.text: Watch the river for an hour

effects.log: Boats, birds, the sun on the water. Nothing in you needs to be written down.

events.text: Upriver from Yichang the great river narrows into the gorges, and trackers haul boats against the current along paths cut into the cliffs, chanting so they all pull at once.

choices.text: Take a place on the tow line

effects.log: You pull all day on a cliff path no wider than a step. At night the trackers share their pepper soup.

choices.text: Ride a boat through the rapids (15 taels)

effects.log: The boat goes through white water between cliffs that touch the sky. You laugh the whole way.

choices.text: Study how the water moves

effects.log: Soft water cut these cliffs. You think about that for a long time.

events.text: At the Dragon Boat Festival the whole river town turns out to race. One crew has lost its drummer to a fever and asks the crowd for anyone who can keep a beat.

choices.text: Beat the drum for them

ok.log: Your drum drives the boat home first by a head. The crew throws you into the river, which is the custom.

fail.log: Your beat drifts and the oars tangle. They come in fourth and throw you in the river anyway.

choices.text: Buy rice dumplings for the crews (8 taels)

effects.log: Leaf-wrapped dumplings for forty rowers. They cheer you louder than the winners.

choices.text: Watch from the bank

effects.log: Drums, spray, the dragons' painted eyes. It is the best day of the summer.

events.text: In the deep forests of Shennongjia, where the herb gatherers go, an old gatherer tells you about the hairy wild people of the mountains, who steal salt and leave footprints as long as an arm.

choices.text: Gather herbs with him

ok.log: You find a root he has looked for all season. He gives you half its price and calls you lucky.

fail.log: You pick a leaf that makes your hands itch for three days. He laughs and shows you the right one.

choices.text: Look for the wild people's footprints

effects.log: You find a footprint in the mud, very large. It might be a bear. You decide it is not.

choices.text: Leave a little salt on a stone

effects.log: In the morning the salt is gone. The gatherer nods as if this proved everything.

events.text: A Wudang Taoist is sweeping the long stair below the Purple Cloud Palace. When you stop to let him pass, he sweeps round your feet instead, without slowing, and smiles.

choices.text: Ask him how he did that

effects.log: "Water goes round a stone," he says. "The stone thinks it won." You walk down the stair thinking about it.

choices.text: Take the second broom and sweep with him

effects.log: You sweep a hundred steps together in silence. Your breathing slows to his.

choices.text: Walk on up the stair

effects.log: At the top you look back. He is still sweeping, and the stair is clean all the way down.

events.text: On a lake near Wuchang a fisherman with cormorants is having a bad day: his best bird has gone off to sit on a lotus leaf and will not come back for anything.

choices.text: Coax the bird back

ok.log: The cormorant looks at you, sighs, and swims back to the boat. The fisherman gives you the day's best fish.

fail.log: The cormorant looks at you, and stays exactly where it is. The fisherman says it does that to everybody.

choices.text: Buy a fish to cheer him (3 taels)

effects.log: He grills it on the boat for both of you. The cormorant comes back for the head.

choices.text: Row on across the lake

effects.log: Lotus, still water, the cry of the birds. The lake goes on and on, and then there is another.

events.text: In the tea hills of the west a widow runs the terraces alone since her son went to the river. Her leaves are ready and the rain is coming.

choices.text: Pick through the night with her

effects.log: You pick by lantern until the rain comes. She roasts the leaves in a great iron pan and gives you a packet.

choices.text: Pay pickers from the village (20 taels)

effects.log: Ten pickers come up the hill with their baskets. The harvest is in before the first drop.

choices.text: Buy a packet of last year's tea

effects.log: You drink it on the road, green and bitter and clean. It is worth every coin.

choices.text: Go on before the rain

effects.log: You reach shelter just as the rain begins. On the hill behind you a lantern moves among the bushes.

events.text: At a little temple to the river god on the bank, the villagers have tied red cloth to every post, because the water is already higher than it should be this early in the year.

choices.text: Pray with them

effects.log: You pray beside an old fisherman who prays like a man arguing with a neighbour. The river listens, or does not.

choices.text: Walk the dike and look for weak places

ok.log: You find two soft places in the earth and show the headman. The village fills them before the rains.

fail.log: The dike all looks the same to you. A child shows you the soft place, kindly.

choices.text: Move on upstream

effects.log: You walk on. Behind you the red cloth flutters on every post.

events.text: The lake children have dared you to swim out to the biggest lotus in the pond and bring back a seed head, without falling off the leaves.

choices.text: Swim out for it

ok.log: You come back with the seed head held up like a lantern. You share the seeds out one by one, the ruler of the pond.

fail.log: You come back with a lotus leaf on your head and a frog in your hair. Everyone agrees it counts.

choices.text: Pole out on a washtub

effects.log: The washtub spins and spins and gets there in the end. You are dizzy and triumphant.

choices.text: Stay on the bank and keep score

effects.log: You keep score so honestly that the others make you the judge of all dares from now on.

events.text: In the square by the river the old men do their slow Wudang forms every morning. One of them waves you over and puts you at the end of the line.

choices.text: Copy the old men

effects.log: You do it too fast, then too slow, then for one breath exactly right. The old man nods once.

choices.text: Ask why they move so slowly

effects.log: "So we notice," says the old man. You do not understand. Years later, you do.

choices.text: Run off to play

effects.log: You run along the river wall with the other children. Behind you the old men turn like reeds in the wind.

events.text: After the autumn rain the paddy edges are full of little crabs, and the village children are catching them in baskets for the market.

choices.text: Catch crabs with them

effects.log: You catch eleven and get pinched twice. Your share of the market money buys a sugar figure.

choices.text: Let your crabs go

effects.log: You tip your basket back into the paddy. The other children think you are mad. The crabs do not.

choices.text: Build the crabs a race track

effects.log: Nobody's crab goes the right way. It is the most fun anyone has had all year.

events.text: On the great river below Wuchang a fast boat with no lamps comes alongside your ferry, and men with hooks begin climbing over the rail while the ferryman hides under his straw cape.

choices.text: Throw them back into the river

ok.log: They go back over the rail faster than they came. The ferry passengers make a collection for you at the landing.

fail.log: You keep them off the women and the children, and lose your purse to the last one over the rail.

choices.text: Steer the ferry into the shallows

ok.log: The pirate boat runs aground on a sandbar behind you. The ferryman comes out from under his cape and kisses the tiller.

fail.log: You run the ferry aground instead. The pirates take what they want and leave you to push off.

choices.text: Hand over your purse

effects.log: They take it and go. The ferryman says it happens every month and nobody does anything.

choices.text: Keep your head down

effects.log: They take the cargo and leave the passengers. You reach the landing with your silver and your shame.

events.text: Floodwater has covered the road between the lakes. A family is stranded on a grave mound in the middle of it, the grandmother, the children and a pig, and the water is still rising.

choices.text: Wade out and carry them over

ok.log: Four trips through the brown water. The pig is the hardest. On the dry road the grandmother bows to the ground.

fail.log: The current knocks you down on the third trip. You get them all over, and lose your pack to the flood.

choices.text: Pay a boatman to fetch them (15 taels)

effects.log: A boatman who was waiting for a better price takes yours instead.

choices.text: Go round by the hills

effects.log: Two days by the high road. You never learn what happened to the family on the mound.

events.text: At dawn your sect gathers on the terrace of the Purple Cloud Palace and moves through the slow forms together, a hundred Taoists turning like one cloud. An elder walks among them with a cup of water on his palm, spilling none.

choices.text: Follow the circle with them

effects.log: For a whole form you forget that you are moving. When you remember, the sun is up.

choices.text: Ask the elder to test your yielding

ok.log: He pushes; you give way and return, and the water in his cup does not move. He smiles. "Again tomorrow," he says.

fail.log: He pushes and you push back. You sit down on the terrace, gently, and his water does not move either.

choices.text: Practise alone on the cliff path

effects.log: Mist below, mist above, and your own breath. It is enough.

events.text: Abbot Qingxu of your sect is teaching the Taiji Sword to a handful of disciples in the pine court. He has not drawn his own sword in thirty years. He uses a willow switch.

choices.text: Learn it from him

effects.log: Circle within circle. He never blocks your blade; he only goes round it. By the end of the month, so do you.

choices.text: Challenge the switch with your sword

ok.log: For three exchanges you keep the willow off you. The abbot laughs aloud, which nobody has heard in years.

fail.log: The willow touches your wrist and your sword is on the ground. "Too much iron," he says.

choices.text: Copy out the sword manual for the library

effects.log: A month of brush and ink. The library keeper writes your name in the merit book.

events.text: The lowland villages below the mountain send a runner up the stairs: the river has broken a dike and they need hands. Your sect's elders are still discussing which disciples to send.

choices.text: Go down without waiting

effects.log: You fill sandbags for three days in the rain. The elders say nothing about the waiting. The villagers say a great deal.

choices.text: Wait for the elders to choose

effects.log: They choose you, in the end. You are a day later, and better organised.

choices.text: Stay and keep the halls

effects.log: Someone must. The palace is very quiet with half the disciples gone.

events.text: A swordsman from a rival sect has climbed to the gate of the Purple Cloud Palace to challenge Wudang in front of the pilgrims. The elders of your sect are all at their meditations, and the duty falls to you.

choices.text: Meet him with the soft and the round

ok.log: Every blow he throws you guide past. In the end he is so tired he sits down on the steps. The pilgrims applaud.

fail.log: He cuts your sleeve and your arm with it, and goes down the stairs boasting. The elders will hear of it.

choices.text: Offer him tea and wait for the elders

effects.log: He drinks three cups, grumbling. By the time the elders come out he has forgotten why he was angry.

choices.text: Tell him Wudang does not fight for show

effects.log: "Then Wudang is afraid," he says. "Then Wudang is alive," you answer. He leaves.

events.text: On the pilgrims' stair below the Purple Cloud Palace a young Taoist of the Wudang Sect falls into step with you. "You walk like someone who would rather go round a wall than through it," she says. "We could teach you the rest."

choices.text: Ask to join the Wudang Sect

effects.log: She takes you to the abbot, who looks at you for a long time and then hands you a broom. You are a Taoist of Wudang.

choices.text: Ask her what Wudang teaches

effects.log: "The soft overcomes the hard," she says, "slowly, and without hurry." You think about it all the way up.

choices.text: Thank her and climb on alone

effects.log: She bows and goes back down the stair. You feel the mountain's quiet follow you.

events.text: The rains will not stop. On the Han River dike, the old dike warden Tan Shouyi is walking the earth with a pole, listening to it the way a doctor listens to a pulse. He asks if you will stay and help him hold it.

choices.text: Stay and fill sandbags

effects.log: You work beside Tan Shouyi until your hands bleed through the cloth. He says nothing, and hands you better gloves.

choices.text: Walk the dike with him

ok.log: You find a leak he missed. He looks at you differently after that.

fail.log: You walk all night and find nothing. He finds two. "Next time," he says.

choices.text: Move on before the road floods

effects.log: You leave before the roads close. Behind you the river is the colour of tea.

events.text: Lord Xue Bingran, who owns half the rice land on the north bank, rides out to the dike with twenty men and spades. If the south bank is cut, he says, the river will spill there and spare his fields. The south bank is where the poor live.

choices.text: Stand in their way

ok.log: Twenty men with spades are not enough. They ride back to Lord Xue to tell him so.

fail.log: They beat you into the mud, but Tan Shouyi and the villagers come with poles, and Lord Xue's men go home.

choices.text: Argue with Lord Xue

ok.log: You tell him the river does not know whose fields are whose. He goes away, not convinced, and not digging.

fail.log: He laughs at you and orders the digging to begin at dawn.

choices.text: Take his silver to look away (100 taels)

effects.log: He pays well. Tan Shouyi watches you take it and turns his back.

events.text: The flood crest comes at night. The dike groans along its whole length, and in the lantern light Tan Shouyi says the south bank will break before morning, with or without Lord Xue's spades.

choices.text: Hold the weak place with your body and qi

ok.log: You stand in the breach with the sandbags all night, the river pushing on your back. At dawn the crest passes, and the dike holds.

fail.log: The breach widens under you and the river takes you a li downstream. The villagers pull you out of a willow tree.

choices.text: Lead the south bank to the hills

ok.log: You get every family up the hill path with lanterns before the dike goes. You count them twice. Nobody is missing.

fail.log: You get most of them up the hill. The river takes the last houses, and the old ferryman's boat, before they are empty.

choices.text: Save yourself

effects.log: You climb to high ground alone. At dawn the south bank is a lake.

events.text: The water goes down. Where the dike held, the south bank villages are mud to the knees and alive. Tan Shouyi sits on the dike in the sun, too tired to stand, and the villagers bring you both rice wine and dried fish and more thanks than you can carry.

choices.text: Help rebuild the dike higher

effects.log: You spend the autumn raising the dike with the villagers. They name the new stretch after you, and argue about the spelling.

choices.text: Eat with Tan Shouyi on the dike

effects.log: He tells you about forty years of floods. You learn that the river is never beaten, only persuaded.

events.text: The south bank is gone under brown water. In the camp on the hill Tan Shouyi is counting the families, slowly, and someone says Lord Xue's fields on the north bank are dry and green.

choices.text: Go and make Lord Xue feed the camp

ok.log: His granary feeds the camp all winter, with you standing at its door. He never forgives you. Nobody else forgets you.

fail.log: His guards drive you off. You spend the winter begging rice for the camp from the other towns.

choices.text: Give the camp what you have (50 taels)

effects.log: It buys rice for a month. Tan Shouyi writes it in his book of the flood without a word.

choices.text: Leave the province

effects.log: You go downriver on the first boat that will take you, and the hill camp watches you go.

events.text: The south bank villages are under the river, and Lord Xue's north bank is green. In the market at Xiangyang they know who took the silver, and an old man spits at your feet. Tan Shouyi is said to have walked into the hills and not come back.

choices.text: Go and find Tan Shouyi

ok.log: You find him in a hermitage on Wudang, sweeping. He hears you out and says, "The river forgives. Go and be useful."

fail.log: You search the mountain for a season and never find him. Something in you stays searching.

choices.text: Spend the silver on a new dike (100 taels)

effects.log: You hire diggers for the south bank. The villagers take your silver and still do not look at you. It is a start.

choices.text: Shrug it off

effects.log: Rivers flood. You leave Hubei richer and lonelier.

events.text: Beside a lotus pond at the foot of Wudang lives an old Taoist named Zhou Wuyan, who left the mountain forty years ago and will not say why. He spends his days pushing a little boat round and round the pond without an oar.
events.arc: The Hermit of the Lotus Pond

choices.text: Ask him how the boat moves

effects.log: "The pond moves," he says. "The boat agrees." He lets you sit on the bank and watch.

choices.text: Bring him rice and say nothing

effects.log: He eats it and says nothing either. When you leave he says, "Come back."

choices.text: Leave the strange old man alone

effects.log: You walk on. The little boat goes round the pond behind you, slow as a clock.

events.text: Zhou Wuyan has decided to teach you, though he will not call it teaching. Every day for a season you carry water from the pond to his hut in a basket, and every day it runs out through the weave.
events.arc: The Hermit of the Lotus Pond

choices.text: Keep carrying it

ok.log: On the last day of the season you carry the basket so smoothly, so fast and so round, that it arrives still wet. He nods.

fail.log: A season of wet sleeves and empty baskets. On the last day he says, "Good," and you do not know why.

choices.text: Weave the basket tighter

effects.log: He watches you do it and laughs until he has to sit down. "Clever," he says. "Wrong, but clever."

choices.text: Give up and go

effects.log: He waves you off with the basket still in his hand. You are not sure who failed.

events.text: A woman in dark grey comes to the pond, a sword on her back and forty years of anger in her face. She is Hong Jiehua, and Zhou Wuyan once killed her teacher in a duel he has regretted every day since. She has come to settle it.
events.arc: The Hermit of the Lotus Pond

choices.text: Stand between them

ok.log: You turn her sword aside three times without striking back, the way the old man taught you. She stops, and looks at him over your shoulder.

fail.log: Her sword goes through your guard and opens your arm. She stops, shocked, and looks at the old man over your shoulder.

choices.text: Ask her to hear his side

ok.log: She lets him speak. It takes all night. In the morning she is still there, and so is her sword, in its sheath.

fail.log: She will not hear it. The old man stands up from his boat and goes to meet her himself.

choices.text: Let them settle it

effects.log: You step back. The old man stands up from his boat and goes to meet her.

events.text: Hong Jiehua puts away her sword. She sits down by the pond beside Zhou Wuyan, and the two old people talk until the lotus close for the night. In the morning she is gone, and he is pushing his boat again, lighter.
events.arc: The Hermit of the Lotus Pond

choices.text: Ask him what she said

effects.log: "That her teacher would have liked you," he says. Then he shows you the form he used that day, so it is not lost.

choices.text: Leave him to his pond

effects.log: You go without asking. When you look back he is waving, the first time he ever has.

events.text: The duel by the pond is short. Neither old sword touches the other: Zhou Wuyan only goes round and round, and in the end Hong Jiehua sits down in the mud and weeps. He sits down beside her. You stay out of sight.
events.arc: The Hermit of the Lotus Pond

choices.text: Bring them both tea

effects.log: They drink it together. Hong Jiehua thanks you without looking at you, which is how such things are done.

choices.text: Go back to the road

effects.log: Some endings are not for strangers. You go quietly, and remember the circle he made.

events.text: In the Wuchang fish market a stout old fishwife, Mother Lu, is being shouted at by the Golden Carp Guild's collector. Her son Lu Xiaoyu borrowed 40 taels for a boat that sank in the spring, and the guild's interest has doubled it.

choices.text: Ask the collector to give her time

ok.log: The collector gives her a month, sourly. Mother Lu gives you a whole bream for nothing.

fail.log: The collector tells you to mind your own fish. Mother Lu tells him to mind his manners.

choices.text: Pay the interest for her (40 taels)

effects.log: The collector takes it and writes something. Mother Lu does not thank you; she gives you a hard look and a bream.

choices.text: Buy a fish and leave them to it

effects.log: The fish is excellent. The shouting follows you halfway down the street.

events.text: Lu Xiaoyu comes to find you, a thin young man smelling of river mud. The Golden Carp Guild owns every boat on the lake, he says, sinks the ones it does not own, and lends money to the men it sinks. He has the boat's broken plank to prove it.

choices.text: Look at the plank

ok.log: Saw marks, neat as writing, on the underside. Someone cut it half through before the boat ever sailed.

fail.log: It looks like a broken plank to you. Lu Xiaoyu takes it back, disappointed.

choices.text: Ask round the other fishermen

effects.log: Five of them have the same story and none of them will say it aloud. They all owe the guild.

choices.text: Tell him it is not your affair

effects.log: He nods as if he expected it, and goes back to the market.

events.text: The guild master, Fang Kui, invites you to his barge on the lake for a dinner of steamed fish. He knows what Lu Xiaoyu has been saying, and he offers you a share in the guild to forget it.

choices.text: Take his hand and his share

effects.log: Fang Kui pours you a cup and calls you brother. The share pays well, every month, in fish money.

choices.text: Turn the dinner into a trial

ok.log: You set the plank on his table in front of his guests, the saw marks up. By morning the whole lake knows.

fail.log: His guests laugh at the plank and his guards throw you off the barge. The lake is cold.

choices.text: Walk out of the dinner

effects.log: You leave his fish untouched. Fang Kui watches you go with a smile you do not like.

events.text: At dawn the fishermen of the lake come to the guild hall with their nets and their debts, and Fang Kui's hired men are waiting with cudgels. Lu Xiaoyu is at the front. Mother Lu is right behind him with a gutting knife she will not put down.

choices.text: Stand at the front with them

ok.log: The hired men break and run. The fishermen burn the guild's ledger of debts in the market square, and Mother Lu feeds the whole street.

fail.log: The cudgels drive you back, but not far. By noon the magistrate comes, and the guild's ledger goes to the court instead of the fire.

choices.text: Take the guild's books to the magistrate

ok.log: The magistrate reads the books, and then reads them again. Fang Kui leaves Wuchang in a closed cart. The debts are struck out.

fail.log: The magistrate owes the guild too. The books disappear. The fishermen settle it with their own hands, and you with them.

events.text: The share comes every month. Then one month Lu Xiaoyu's new boat sinks, the way the old one did, and Mother Lu comes to your door and stands there without speaking. She does not have to.

choices.text: Give the share to Mother Lu (120 taels)

effects.log: She takes it and leaves without a word. The next week a bream arrives at your door, and every week after.

choices.text: Close the door

effects.log: You close it. Word goes round the lake about you, and every fish seller in Wuchang turns away.
